commit_message_on_validation:
- S2.42: a named constant of character or numeric value is the operand
  of its value, as eval's `Sym::Const(c) => c`. The value goes into
  the routine's layout lines. The compiled code names the constant,
  not its value, so two programs with the same calculations and
  different constants would otherwise share generated code. Section
  7's native-diff found this (rla_test
  include_search_order_follows_source_kind), and NCONSTA and NCONSTB
  now test it.
- S2.43: settle and the native call note and route a program error
  with the fork's own code. It is written again from errors.rs
  note_error, psds_error, passes_by and the PSDS helpers, and from
  interp.rs sender: %STATUS, %ERROR, the PSDS and the exception message
  in the call message queue. File errors (1000 and up) still go to the
  interpreter's note_error, for its file state. native_tripwire.rs now
  watches every interpreter function written again since S2.35.
- S2.44: EVAL with %SUBST as its target, in the interpreter's order.
  A negative or past-the-end start or length is RNQ0100, never a
  panic. Expected values come from IBM's documentation ("%SUBST Used
  as the Result of an Assignment"), in NSUBT.
- docs/native/evidence/2026-11-15-s241.json records the previous
  commit's section 7.

Section 7 on this tree (snapshot 4812103, the catalog::init lock fix
